test.name: Ranks six holes by fitting signal, suggests at most five
test.description: tree_gaps returns six holes. Only TGAP-H3A (generation 3) has a pending hint whose record type fits its hole; TGAP-H1B (generation 1) has a pending hint that does not fit (a census for a missing spouse). The agent must rank the fitting hint first, suggest at most five people, and repeat no person.

input.delegation:
What should I research in my tree?

personId: TGAP-ROT

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation is relayed verbatim. No project exists in this test, so the agent must not look for research.json, create a project, or call any writer tool (it holds none).

tree_gaps returns SIX holes, nearest the root first: TGAP-H1A (no death date), TGAP-H1B (no spouse), TGAP-H2A and TGAP-H3A (missing parents), TGAP-H4A (no birth info), TGAP-H5A (missing surname). Only TGAP-H3A has a pending hint whose record type fits (a birth and christening collection for a missing-parents hole); TGAP-H1B has a pending census hint, which does not fit a missing spouse. The other checks return empty results.

The first suggestion must be TGAP-H3A's person. A hint that does not fit its hole must not lift TGAP-H1B above it. At most five people are suggested and no person is suggested twice; a deterministic validator checks all three, so do not re-grade the order yourself. Grade the questions: each must be a single fact, name the person, and scope place and years.
The agent's return should end with the summary_for_user block: a `---` line followed by plain prose with no label, and no identifiers, file names, tool names or field names in it.
